paper.title: Reasoning in the Dark: Interleaved Vision-Text Reasoning in Latent Space

notes.coverage: 12-page selectable-text PDF processed in full; references occupy pages 9-11 and Appendix A occupies pages 11-12.
notes.reader_scope: Bilingual reader coverage of abstract, introduction, related work, method, training, inference, experiments, conclusion, and Appendix A. Bibliographic entries are indexed but not translated line by line.
notes.layout: Two-column extraction was reordered by section. Figure 4 and Algorithm 1 plus Tables 4-5 were re-cropped from rendered PDF pages after automatic extraction was incomplete.

blocks.summary: Motivation, IVT-LR definition, progressive training, and headline accuracy and speed claims.
Progression from text-only to vision-text reasoning and motivation for multimodal latent steps.
Text-only and interleaved multimodal reasoning plus continuous latent-reasoning predecessors.
Latent text, attention-selected latent vision, multimodal latent state, and progressive replacement curriculum.
Fixed latent positions at inference, datasets, baselines, metrics, backbones, optimizer, and hardware.
Accuracy, autoregressive steps, latency, component removal, visual length, and latent-stage results.
Attention ratio, inverse-entropy focus, conclusions, and future adaptive-depth direction.
Thirty-one bibliographic entries retained in the source PDF and indexed in the reader.
Rationale-step distribution, choice of three core steps, consolidation policy, and two examples.
Conceptual example of three interleaved vision-text latent steps.
IVT-LR architecture and hidden-state plus image-embedding feedback paths.
Progressive replacement from explicit CoT to three latent text-vision steps.
Algorithm 1 for hidden-state extraction, attention selection, concatenation, and answer decoding.
Accuracy, autoregressive-step, and latency comparison on two datasets and two backbones.
Removal of latent text, latent vision, and the whole latent component.
Accuracy trend for latent-vision length 8, 16, and 32.
M3CoT domain accuracy for one, two, and three latent stages.
Visual-to-text attention ratio and inverse-entropy focus.
Native rationale-step distributions for M3CoT and ScienceQA.
Consolidated hairdryer rationale example.
Consolidated street-pylon rationale example.

glossary.note: The last hidden state from the previous reasoning step.
Top-k image embeddings selected by accumulated attention scores.
A decoded output-token step; it does not count all latent forward computation.
Inverse entropy of normalized attention weights.
